description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by undergraduate/graduate level, sex, and race/ethnicity. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and enrollment level (EFFYLEV); this 2006-07 table uses the old race/ethnicity categories, including nine categories.

12-month instructional activity measured in total credit hours and/or contact hours, reported separately for undergraduate and graduate activity. Query this table for instructional-volume measures used to derive 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment, rather than unduplicated student headcounts.

Awards and degrees conferred from July 1, 2006, through June 30, 2007, reported by postsecondary institutions in the IPEDS Completions universe (Title IV-participating institutions). Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, six-digit CIPCODE, MAJORNUM (first or second major), and AWLEVEL (certificate or degree level). The table provides total awards and awards by gender and the nine old race/ethnicity categories; 2006-07 was the final year all institutions reported using those old race/ethnicity categories.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and attendance status and level of student (EFLEVEL), with total and male/female counts, including full- and part-time counts.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and attendance status and level of student (EFALEVEL); Fall 2007 uses the old race/ethnicity categories, the last year they were reported by all institutions.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY). Age-based enrollment is optional in even-numbered years, so 2007 (odd) has data under the catalog’s reporting rule.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including the number who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and state of residence (EFCSTATE). Residence-based enrollment is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2007 (odd) has data under the catalog’s reporting rule.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio. The measures apply only to institutions with undergraduate students; entering-class data are reported only by academic-year institutions, and institutions offering short programs of less than one year do not have retention data.

Institutional revenues by source, expenditures by function and natural classification, and assets and liabilities for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards. The row grain is the reporting public institution; it does not cover FASB-reporting public institutions, private not-for-profit institutions, or component units.

Assets, liabilities, and net assets for legally separate component units of public GASB institutions that use FASB accounting standards. Records are identified by the primary institution and component-unit entity, with the entity name and its general nature also reported; component-unit financial data are available for fiscal years 2002 through 2007.

Assets, liabilities, and net assets for legally separate component units of public GASB institutions that use GASB accounting standards. Records are identified by the primary institution and component-unit entity, with the entity name and its general nature also reported; component-unit financial data are available for fiscal years 2002 through 2007.

Institutional revenues by source, expenditures by function and natural classification, and assets and liabilities for all private not-for-profit institutions plus public institutions that use FASB accounting standards. The row grain is the reporting institution, so this is the FASB-based institutional-finance table rather than the public GASB form or the private for-profit form.

Institutional revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards. The row grain is the reporting for-profit institution; it is separate from the FASB table for private not-for-profit and public institutions.

Graduation-rate outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at four-year and two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely defined by UNITID and GRTYPE (cohort and graduation status): four-year records cover the 2001 cohort, including bachelor’s-degree seekers and students seeking other awards, with bachelor’s completion milestones at 100%, 125%, and 150% of normal time; two-year records cover the 2004 cohort and include completion of any degree/certificate within 150% and transfer-out counts.

Graduation and transfer outcomes for the full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohort at less-than-2-year institutions, for the 2004 cohort. The institution-level record is identified by UNITID and contains cohort enrollment, completion within 150% of normal time, and transfer-out counts.

Fall staff counts broken down by occupational category, full- or part-time status, medical school status, and faculty tenure status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPRECTP, which combines occupational category, tenure status, and full-/part-time status.

Full- and part-time employees on the November 1 payroll, broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SABDTYPE, which defines occupational category and full-/part-time status; race/ethnicity uses the old categories, which were last used for all institutions in Fall 2007. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2007 (odd) has data available.

Employees in degree-granting institutions with fewer than 15 full-time employees and in all nondegree-granting institutions, broken down by primary function or occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SCNLEVEL, which defines the primary function or occupation; race/ethnicity uses the old categories, which were last used for all institutions in Fall 2007. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2007 (odd) has data available.

Full-time instruction, research, and public-service staff in degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees, broken down by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK, which combines faculty status and academic rank; race/ethnicity uses the old categories, which were last used for all institutions in Fall 2007. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2007 (odd) has data available.

Full-time new hires in degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees, broken down by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SGTYPE, which defines the primary occupation; race/ethnicity uses the old categories, which were last used for all institutions in Fall 2007. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2007 (odd) has data available.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff broken down by gender, academic rank, and contract length. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID, ARANK, and CONTRACT.
Counts of full-time, nonmedical instructional faculty with contracts shorter than 9 months, broken down by gender and academic rank. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK.

Fringe-benefit participation, total expenditures, and average expenditures for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by contract length and benefit-plan type. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and BENTYPE.

Full-time, nonmedical instructional staff counts in 4-year institutions broken down by faculty status, contract length, and academic rank. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID, CONTRACT, and ARANK.

Response and applicability status by institution and survey component, including whether data were submitted, imputed, or revised and whether the institution reports as a parent or child in a multiple-campus arrangement. The row grain is institution by survey component.

Directory information for each institution, including identifying and contact details, web links, active status, Title IV participation, control and institutional level, highest award offered, and Carnegie classifications. The row grain is one institution.

Institution-level offerings, organization and control, affiliations, special learning opportunities, services, and athletic associations, along with applicant, admission, and test-score measures. Admissions and test-score fields are restricted to institutions that do not have an open-admissions policy; the row grain is one institution.

Student charges for full-academic-year programs at institutions using semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or another academic-year calendar. The institution-level table includes tuition and required fees for full-time undergraduate and graduate students, per-credit-hour charges for part-time undergraduate and graduate students, first-professional charges, and published price of attendance for full-time first-time undergraduates.

Student charges for vocational or other programs reported by full program length at institutions using clock-hour programs or primarily occupational credit-hour programs. The institution-level record identifies the number of programs and charges for the largest program plus up to five additional program slots, including tuition and fees and books and supplies; price of attendance is reported for entering students in the largest program.
The mission statement for each institution or a web address leading to its mission statement. The row grain is one institution.

Student financial aid counts and average aid amounts for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, separated by aid type and source, including federal, state/local, institutional grants, and student loans. The table is institution-by-aid-source/type in grain, with recipient counts and average dollars; it covers the stated July 1, 2007–June 30, 2008 reporting period for the 2006-07 aid year and is available in this odd-numbered 2007 collection.
